title: Revenue Accounting Note on Flown Coupons, Ticket Status and No-Shows
content:
**Revenue accounting note — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** Each flown segment consumes its coupon value from the ticket: the coupon entry records the segment number, flight number, flight date and cabin flown, and moves that segment's share of the fare out of the ticket value.

## Coupons and status

- A coupon is flown only on a ticket that is ticketed or partially flown.
- The first flown coupon of a multi-segment ticket moves it to partially flown, and the final coupon moves it to flown. The only coupon of a single-segment ticket moves it straight to flown.
- Every flown coupon passes to the passenger's Summit membership for accrual on the fare brand's earning basis: qualifying dollars on the fare brand's qualifying-dollar percent of the segment fare, and a cabin bonus of the fare brand's cabin bonus percent of the base award miles. The per-dollar earning rates belong to the loyalty program.

## No-shows

A passenger who neither cancels before the cancellation cutoff nor boards is a no-show, and the remaining itinerary is cancelled.

| Fare brand treatment of unflown value | Ticket after the no-show | Unflown value |
|---|---|---|
| Forfeited in full | Forfeited | The entire residual value is forfeited, ground no-show |
| Retained on the ticket | Remains ticketed, for a later cancellation or refund | Stays on the ticket |

A passenger who missed a flight because of a Crestline disruption recorded on that segment is reaccommodated and is never treated as a no-show.

## Status conditions on retentions

A no-show forfeiture is booked only on a ticket whose status is forfeited, and a cancellation-fee retention only on a ticket whose status is cancelled to credit.

*Hypothetical case.* A Crestline Main Cabin passenger with a residual value of 210.00 dollars misses the flight without cancelling and without any disruption on record: the ticket becomes forfeited and 210.00 dollars is forfeited. The same facts on Crestline First leave the 210.00 dollars on the still-ticketed ticket.
